author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
The AI labs are running out of useful things to work on.

I think most people already assume all those maths/physics problems are true and live with it. Proving them really are true doesn't change anything to our daily life.

author.name: Mark Gantlett
author.headline: Principal Systems Architect & Founder, Gantlett Systems Inc. | Deterministic Control Systems Beneath Enterprise AI Coding Tools (Nomos Open-Core)

comments.text: The theorems themselves do not change daily life, true. Coming from silicon you probably see the real signal underneath though: a formal verifier kept an agent loop honest across thousands of steps. That same verify-first loop applied to everyday software and hardware builds is where the actual payoff sits.

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Using AI building the chips that power the AI.

replies.text: Mark Gantlett Yeah. We have the agent loop, it works OK, then we run into the Rice's Therom
